title: An Additive Manufacturing Technique for the Facile and Rapid Fabrication of Hydrogel-based Micromachines with Magnetically Responsive Components
protocol: Assemble the fabrication stage with an in-house built setup including an acrylic top, tracks and channels for vacuum connections, holder for micrometer head, and threaded steel posts.
Fix the micrometer head using an acrylic piece machined for vacuum connection.
Position a UV light source above the fabrication stage to ensure perpendicular incidence on the horizontal plane of the stage.
Make a PDMS chamber in which hydrogels will be polymerized.
Prepare a 9:1 weight ratio mixture of PDMS base and curing agent.
Stir well with a glass rod to ensure that the base and curing agents are well mixed.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g to remove air bubbles.
Carefully pour the PDMS mixture into two glass Petri dishes to yield a thick layer (~3 mm) and a thin layer (~0.2 mm).
Place PDMS-filled Petri dishes on a flat, level surface and cure overnight at room temperature or for 30 minutes in an oven with temperature set at a minimum of 75 °C.
Cut a 4 cm diameter circle into the thick layer using a scalpel blade or penknife.
Peel the thick PDMS layer off from the glass Petri dish.
Place the thick PDMS layer (bottom-side up) and the thin PDMS layer (still in the glass Petri dish) into a plasma oven.
Plasma treat the two PDMS layers (30 s, air plasma).
Bond the bottom side of the thick PDMS layer to the top-side of the thin PDMS layer.
Plasma treat both the glass coverslip and PDMS chamber for 30 s (air plasma).
Place the glass coverslip in contact with the top-side of the flexible membrane base to bond it to the membrane.
Vapor silanize the PDMS chamber with trichloro (1H, 1H, 2H, 2H-perfluorooctyl) silane for at least 30 minutes.
Place the PDMS chamber in a vacuum desiccator along with a small Petri dish containing 60 µL of PFOTS.
Connect the sealed desiccator to the central laboratory vacuum system and leave it connected for at least 30 minutes.
Ensure that the vacuum seal of the desiccator is generated and that the droplet of PFOTS "bubbles" after 5 - 10 minutes.
Place the PDMS chamber on a vacuum-enabled stage connected to the laboratory central vacuum system.
Apply negative pressure to hold the PDMS chamber down.
Place an untreated glass coverslip on top of the PDMS chamber such that it covers the well.
Push the bottom substrate upwards until it is in contact with the top substrate using the micrometer head.
Use the reading on the micrometer head as the "zero" level of the PDMS chamber.
Design photomasks for each unique layer of the hydrogel structure to be fabricated using CAD software.
Incorporate alignment marks into the photomask designs to facilitate alignment during fabrication.
Print the designs as transparency photomasks at the highest resolution available and at high pixel densities.
Treat glass coverslips to prevent adhesion of hydrogels.
Prepare PDMS at a 9:1 base to curing agent ratio.
Centrifuge PDMS at 1,000 x g to remove air bubbles.
Apply a thin coat of PDMS to cleaned glass coverslips.
Cure the coated coverslips on a flat, level surface within an oven (>75 °C, 30 min).
Use an untreated piece of glass coverslip (No.2) as a "lid" for the PDMS chamber.
Lower the bottom substrate using the micrometer head to the desired height.
Deposit a small volume of PEGDA prepolymer sufficient to cover the bottom substrate.
Place the top substrate onto the PDMS chamber.
Ensure no air bubbles are trapped between the top and bottom substrates.
Place a photomask with the desired design on top of the top substrate.
Ensure the mask is in full contact with the top substrate and aligned to the bottom substrate.
Expose the hydrogel prepolymer to UV light through the photomask.
Wear UV protection when operating the system.
Lift the top substrate off the PDMS chamber after polymerization.
Reserve the adhered polymerized layer for later use.
Shield the polymerized layer from light.
Keep the polymerized layer wet with excess uncrosslinked prepolymer.
Deposit more hydrogel prepolymer onto the bottom substrate.
Cover the PDMS well with a PDMS-coated glass coverslip.
Repeat steps 5.1.4 and 5.1.5 with the desired photomask design.
Remove the top substrate.
Add more PEGDA prepolymer.
Lower the bottom substrate to the desired level for the second layer of hydrogel.
Cover the PDMS well with the top substrate (PDMS-coated glass).
Repeat steps 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.
Continually build up layers of hydrogel as desired using steps 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 until the desired support structures are formed.
Remove the top substrate (PDMS-coated glass).
Place pre-formed hydrogel components onto the support structures using tweezers.
Bring the bottom substrate to the final desired height using the micrometer screw gauge.
Place the pre-formed hydrogel layer adhered onto the untreated glass coverslip onto the partially assembled device.
Align the hydrogel layer correctly with the structures below it.
Place a photomask that allows for sealing of the device but protects interior moving components from UV exposure.
Expose the entire structure to UV light.
Lift the glass coverslip from the fabrication stage.
Ensure the sealed device adheres to the top substrate.
Carefully lift the device with flat-tipped tweezers or a flat spatula if it remains adhered to the bottom substrate.
Remove excess unpolymerized PEGDA using vacuum suction.
Carefully lift the device off the glass coverslip using flat-tipped tweezers or a flat spatula.
Place the device into saline solution or DI water.
Leave the device in solution for at least 30 minutes to allow stabilization and expansion.
Rinse and leach off any uncrosslinked prepolymers by changing the solution every hour (at least 3 rinses) and leaving overnight if the device is for in vivo implantation.
Place the device within a Petri dish filled with DI water or saline within a vacuum chamber connected to central laboratory vacuum systems for at least 30 minutes.
Keep the device hydrated/in solution at all times to prevent cracking due to drying out.
Prepare a PEGDA prepolymer solution with 1% photoinitiator (99% (v/v) PEGDA (400 Da) with 1% Darocur 1173).
Weigh out 5 mg of iron oxide nanoparticles and add 100 µL of PEGDA prepolymer.
Pipette up and down and vortex to ensure uniform mixing.
Ensure that nanoparticles are homogenously dispersed within the PEGDA prepolymer before each use.
Pipette a small volume of the iron oxide - PEGDA prepolymer mixture onto the bottom substrate of the PDMS chamber.
Cover the PDMS well with the top substrate (PDMS-coated glass).
Bring the bottom substrate to the desired height using the micrometer head.
Expose the thin layer of iron oxide-doped prepolymer to UV light through a photomask defining the shape of the segment.
Increase UV exposure time (~10 seconds) to ensure full cross-linking of the iron-doped segment.
Lower the bottom substrate and repeat steps 5-6, building the iron-doped segment in thin layers each time to the desired height.
Remove any excess iron-doped prepolymer using vacuum suction after completing the iron-doped segment.
Deposit PEGDA prepolymer onto the polymerized iron-doped segment.
Bring the bottom substrate to the final height of the component to be completed.
Cover the PDMS well with a top substrate (PDMS-coated glass).
Expose the PEGDA prepolymer and the iron-doped segment to UV light using a photomask that defines the entire shape of the moving component.
Remove the top substrate.
Use vacuum suction to remove excess unpolymerized PEGDA prepolymer.
Gently lift the PEG component with an iron-oxide doped segment from the bottom substrate using tweezers.
Reserve the iron-doped component for assembly onto support structures of a PEG-based device.
Shield the component from light and ensure it remains wetted with uncrosslinked prepolymer before use.
Place a neodymium magnet below or above the device within 1 - 2 cm away from the device.
Move the magnet to induce movement in the iron-oxide doped components.
Use an actuator built with a motor attached to a magnet for rotational actuation of the iron-doped component.
